boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Hoke's Run record (July 2, 1861) in Manassas Campaign [July 1861]. Patterson's crossing at Williamsport, the July 3 occupation of Martinsburg and his later movements to Bunker Hill, Charlestown and Harper's Ferry are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. NPS says Abercrombie's and Thomas's brigades met regiments of Jackson's brigade. Jackson says only one regiment and one gun of his command were brought into action and quotes Harper that he carried 380 men into the fight. Patterson says the force scattered was 3,500 strong, and on July 4 puts Johnston seven miles ahead with 15,000-18,000 foot, 22 guns and 650 horse, a force 'claimed in all to be thirty thousand ; in reality, thirteen thousand' after joining Bee.
claims.rationale: Patterson's figures describe different populations and dates from Jackson's engaged regiment. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General Thomas J. Jackson and Major General Robert Patterson; the live page gives Jackson as Major General, and Jackson signs as colonel of Virginia volunteers. Jackson says he directed Harper's regiment and Pendleton's battery and ordered the withdrawal under his instructions; Stuart's cavalry captured a Pennsylvania company. Patterson reports the pursuit to Martinsburg.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; no automatic sole credit and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says the Union brigades drove Jackson's regiments back slowly and he withdrew before the larger force; Jackson says he fell back as his orders required, having accomplished his purposes; Patterson says he scattered the force and pursued. NPS's statements that Patterson's later retrograde freed Johnston and contributed to the defeat at First Manassas describe campaign contribution, not this engagement's tactical result.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 114 (US 23; CS 91); the live field reads 98 (US 73; CS 25). Patterson puts the Confederate loss at about sixty killed. Jackson quotes Harper's report of eleven wounded and nine missing and several believed dead, eight Union dead found, and Stuart's forty-nine prisoners taken with one of his own wounded and two missing.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: The Union subordinate reports (Thomas, Perkins, Keim, Abercrombie, Starkweather, Jarrett, Hudson, Simpson), Johnston's transmittal and the June 28-30 returns were read (the Confederate abstract is garbled) but not selected. Nicolay's Chapter XIII mentions the skirmish at Falling Waters only in one clause and was not used.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Patterson's July 3 and 4, 1861 dispatches (Official Records Series I, Volume II) are one family of interested Union accounts. T. J. Jackson's July 3, 1861 report (same volume) is one family of interested Confederate accounts. No Scribner history narrates the skirmish beyond a single clause in Nicolay. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
